summary: Partial KV shard metadata gap forces cold-path lookup for identical replay requests, causing FBT/regression and occasional timeouts
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 06:20 UTC, LinguaFlow reported higher first-byte latency (FBT) and intermittent 504 stream disconnects for identical 'replay' chat turns that previously hit the hot prefix cache. Impact: User-facing slowdown on conversational replay flows; p99 FBT increased from ~300ms to ~2s for identical prompts, with ~0.6% of requests hitting 504 stream timeouts during micro-bursts. Environment: Dedicated customer cluster in us-east running gptx-13b-v1 model variants. Observed pattern: The regression affects sequences where the client resends an identical prompt (replay/undo-redo UX) within 5–20s of the prior turn. Instead of a hot-key KV cache hit, some requests take a cold-path multi-shard lookup, increasing token-generation startup time and occasionally triggering the streaming connection to disconnect. This appears correlated with background shard metadata refreshes and a prefetch worker window that briefly returns stale or partial shard maps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LinguaFlow replay workload (identical 512-token prompt) with concurrency 8 from us-east. 2) Send same prompt twice with 10s gap. 3) Observe streaming latency for second request. 4) Repeat across 50 iterations to reproduce p99 spikes. Expected: second request should hit KV prefix cache hotpath and have FBT similar to first. Actual: occasional fallback to cold lookup with FBT jump and sometimes 504 if downstream streaming buffer times out.

Sample logs (abridged):
[2026-03-12T06:21:17.842Z] request_id=rf-4a9 shard_map_version=v17 cache_lookup=partial-miss prefetch_worker=busy route=hot-path->fallback fbt=2137ms stream=closed(504)
[2026-03-12T06:21:27.120Z] request_id=rf-4a9 shard_map_version=v17 kv_index_shards=[s1,s2,-] kv_lookup=multi-shard cold_path=true
[2026-03-12T06:22:01.009Z] request_id=rf-7f2 shard_map_version=v18 cache_lookup=hit fbt=312ms stream=ok
Observability notes: most partial-miss events have 'kv_index_shards' containing a '-' placeholder indicating missing shard mapping; these cluster around times when the shard-metadata agent logs a reindex cycle (v16->v18).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a short-lived race between the shard metadata update and the kvcache prefetch worker can create a mapping hole for certain prefixes. When the mapping hole is observed the request falls back to a cold-path multi-shard lookup (synchronous) rather than the async hot prefix fetch, increasing FBT and sometimes exceeding streaming timeouts. Evidence: correlated timestamps between 'shard-metadata:reindex' events and spike windows; traces show additional 1.2s spent waiting on sequential shard lookups. Alternative hypotheses considered: noisy neighbor GPU stalls, network packet loss, or client-side retries — none correlated with observed windows. Reproduction proved deterministic when we forced a metadata refresh during warm cache conditions. Additional note: impact disproportionately affects replay (identical) flows because they expect hot prefix KV hits and have tighter client-side streaming timeouts.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported increase in p99 FBT and some 504 disconnects for identical replay requests. Collected request IDs and initial traces, escalating to SRE.

Marcus Chen (SRE): Confirmed correlation with shard-metadata reindex events. Created temporary alert rule to detect 'partial-miss' token in access logs and raised priority. Kicking off deep-dive with runtime team.

Lena Ortiz (Runtime Eng): Found race in metadata swap: new shardmap published before in-memory index update completed on some nodes, leading to '-' placeholders in kvcatalog. Adding blocking step in apply path to avoid partial maps. Planning patch and canary rollout to a subset of dedicated clusters.

Marcus Chen (SRE): Workaround applied: extended metadata application window to force in-sync index, enabled conservative prefetch backoff for 15s in affected cluster. Customer observed immediate reduction in 504s. Monitoring continues.
Customer (LinguaFlow - Support Contact): Noted immediate improvement after workaround. Asked for permanent fix timeline and postmortem.
resolution: Workaround: temporarily blocked metadata swap until in-memory index build completed (deployed 2026-03-12 12:40 UTC) and applied conservative prefetch backoff on affected nodes. Root cause: race between shard metadata publication and local index application produced partial shard mappings for some prefixes; requests hitting those partial maps fell back to synchronous multi-shard cold lookups, increasing FBT and causing stream timeouts. Fix: runtime change to make metadata swap atomic (ensure index built then flip), plus safety check that rejects published mapping that would create '-' placeholders. Patch PR created and under review: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5172. Rollout plan: canary to 10% of dedicated clusters 2026-03-14, full rollout 2026-03-17 after validation. Postmortem and follow-ups: add canary metric, improve alerting for 'partial-miss' rate, update KV cache runbook.
